title: Driver Frontal Stage 1 Deployment Control
plain: The airbag computer found a problem in the circuit that fires the driver's front airbag (first stage). The driver's airbag may not deploy in a crash.
symptoms: Horn or steering wheel buttons may stop working if the clock spring is the cause

causes.name: Worn clock spring (the coiled wire inside the steering column)
Loose connector behind the steering wheel airbag
Faulty driver airbag
Airbag control module fault

checks: Check your VIN for open airbag recalls at NHTSA.gov
Have an airbag-capable scan tool read all airbag codes
Make sure nothing under the front seats is pulling on the wiring (don't unplug the yellow connectors)
fix: A trained technician repairs the wiring or connector, or replaces the faulty part, then clears the code and checks the light goes out.
drive: The car drives normally, but the airbags may not deploy in a crash. Have it checked right away by a shop with an airbag scanner, and check your VIN for open recalls.
test_first: Don't unplug, probe or remove airbag parts or the yellow connectors yourself; an airbag can deploy and cause serious injury. A trained technician should power the system down the way the service manual says and read every airbag code with an airbag-capable scan tool before replacing anything.

Wiring pinched by the seat track
Faulty side airbag
Airbag control module fault

title: First Row Center Seatbelt Load Limiter Deployment Control
plain: The airbag computer found a problem in the circuit for a front-row seat belt load limiter. A load limiter lets the belt give a little in a crash to reduce chest injuries. The seat belt still holds, but this crash feature may not work.

causes.name: Loose or damaged connector at the seat belt or under the seat
Wiring problem
Faulty seat belt assembly
Airbag control module fault

checks: Check your VIN for open airbag recalls at NHTSA.gov
Have an airbag-capable scan tool read all airbag codes
Make sure nothing under the front seats is pulling on the wiring (don't unplug the yellow connectors)
fix: A trained technician repairs the wiring or connector, or replaces the faulty part, then clears the code and checks the light goes out.
drive: The car drives normally and the seat belt still holds, but the airbags and seat belt crash features may not work right in a crash. Always wear your belt. Have it checked right away by a shop with an airbag scanner, and check your VIN for open recalls.
test_first: Don't unplug, probe or remove airbag parts or the yellow connectors yourself; an airbag can deploy and cause serious injury. A trained technician should power the system down the way the service manual says and read every airbag code with an airbag-capable scan tool before replacing anything.

title: Left Side Restraints Sensor 2
plain: The airbag computer has a problem with one of the crash sensors on the left side of the car. Side crash sensors tell the computer when to fire the side airbags, so they may not deploy in a side crash.

causes.name: Faulty side crash sensor in the door or pillar
Water in the door getting into the sensor connector
Wiring damaged in the door hinge area
Damage from an earlier side collision

checks: Check your VIN for open airbag recalls at NHTSA.gov
Have an airbag-capable scan tool read all airbag codes
Make sure nothing under the front seats is pulling on the wiring (don't unplug the yellow connectors)
fix: A trained technician repairs the wiring or connector, or replaces the faulty part, then clears the code and checks the light goes out.
drive: The car drives normally, but the airbags may not deploy in a crash. Have it checked right away by a shop with an airbag scanner, and check your VIN for open recalls.
test_first: Don't unplug, probe or remove airbag parts or the yellow connectors yourself; an airbag can deploy and cause serious injury. title: Occupant Classification System
plain: The system that senses who is in the front passenger seat (an adult, a child or no one) has a fault. It decides whether the passenger airbag should be on or off, so the airbag may be off when it should be on, or on when it should be off.
symptoms: The passenger airbag on/off light doesn't match who is in the seat

causes.name: Faulty seat sensor mat or occupant classification module
Loose connector under the passenger seat
Heavy objects or a seat cover confusing the sensor
Sensor needs re-zeroing after seat work

checks: Check your VIN for open airbag recalls at NHTSA.gov
Take heavy items and aftermarket seat covers off the passenger seat
Have an airbag-capable scan tool read the codes and check the occupant sensor
fix: A trained technician repairs the wiring or connector, or replaces the faulty part, then clears the code and checks the light goes out.
drive: The car drives normally, but the passenger airbag may not deploy in a crash, or may deploy when it shouldn't. Until it's fixed, have children 12 and under ride in the back seat. Have it checked right away by a shop with an airbag scanner, and check your VIN for open recalls.
test_first: Don't unplug, probe or remove airbag parts or the yellow connectors yourself; an airbag can deploy and cause serious injury. A trained technician should power the system down the way the service manual says and read every airbag code with an airbag-capable scan tool before replacing anything.
